info.text:
Wrongly claim head of household? The IRS can bill it back, plus up to 20%.
For 2025 returns, the standard deduction is $15,750 for single filers and $23,625 for head of household.
Head of household requires being unmarried (or considered unmarried), paying over half the home's costs, and a qualifying person living with you.
Claiming it wrongly means at least about $945 underpaid in the 12% bracket (from the deduction alone), which the IRS can bill back with interest and a possible 20% penalty ($189).
Fix mistakes with Form 1040-X, generally within 3 years.
Sources: IRS Publication 501; IRS 2026 inflation adjustments; IRC sec. 6662.
News and education, not financial advice.
